stages.name: Your Cancer Profile
stages.plain_language: CrisPRO reads your medical reports — CT scans, pathology results, genetic tests — and builds a complete picture of your cancer. This includes your tumor type, stage, biomarker test results, and genetic mutations. Think of it as a organized summary of everything your doctors know about your cancer, all in one place.

items.label: MSI status
items.what_it_means: Your tumor has stable microsatellites. This means checkpoint immunotherapy alone is unlikely to work for you.

items.label: PD-L1
items.what_it_means: Your tumor has some immune checkpoint protein, which could make certain immunotherapy combinations worth exploring.

items.label: TP53
items.what_it_means: TP53 mutation is common in high-grade serous ovarian cancer and helps confirm your diagnosis.

items.label: Genetic test
items.what_it_means: You have an inherited genetic mutation in the MBD4 gene. This is rare and may increase risk for certain blood cancers and colon cancer. Your family may benefit from genetic counseling.

items.label: BRCA/HRD
items.what_it_means: Testing for BRCA mutations and HRD (homologous recombination deficiency) is strongly recommended. These results determine whether PARP inhibitor drugs could work for you.

data_shown.completeness_explanation: Your profile is 55% complete. You have pathology and genetic testing, but are missing tumor sequencing (NGS), CA-125 levels, and BRCA/HRD testing. Getting these tests could unlock more treatment options.

stages.name: Biomarker Intelligence: What Your Test Results Mean
stages.plain_language: Each biomarker test result tells a story about your tumor. CrisPRO translates these results into plain language — what each marker means, which treatments it connects to, and what questions to ask your doctor. For example, your MSS status means immunotherapy alone probably won't work, but your PD-L1 positivity and MBD4 mutation suggest specific combination approaches might be worth discussing.

biomarkers.what_it_means: Your tumor's DNA doesn't have enough mutations to attract the immune system on its own. This is why single-agent immunotherapy hasn't worked well for MSS tumors.
biomarkers.questions_to_ask: Are there clinical trials testing immunotherapy combinations for MSS ovarian cancer?

biomarkers.what_it_means: Your tumor expresses a protein that can be targeted by checkpoint inhibitors. A CPS of 10 is moderate — not high enough to guarantee response, but not zero either.
biomarkers.treatments_connected: Pembrolizumab, nivolumab (checkpoint inhibitors) — likely in combination
biomarkers.questions_to_ask: Would adding a checkpoint inhibitor to my chemotherapy be beneficial given my PD-L1 status?

biomarkers.what_it_means: MBD4 is involved in DNA repair. Loss of MBD4 function may make tumors more sensitive to certain DNA-damaging drugs and immunotherapy approaches. This is a rare finding being actively researched.
biomarkers.questions_to_ask: Are there clinical trials specifically for MBD4-mutated tumors? Does this affect my PARP inhibitor eligibility?

biomarkers.what_it_means: This is the most important missing test for ovarian cancer. BRCA mutations and HRD status determine whether PARP inhibitors (olaparib, niraparib) could work for you. About 50% of high-grade serous ovarian cancers have HRD.
biomarkers.questions_to_ask: Can we order BRCA1/2 and HRD testing? This could open up maintenance therapy options.

stages.name: Finding Clinical Trials For You
stages.plain_language: CrisPRO searches clinical trial databases and matches your profile against ongoing trials. It looks at your cancer type, stage, biomarkers, treatment history, and genetic mutations to find trials you may be eligible for. Each trial is ranked by how well it fits your specific situation.

data_shown.how_it_works: CrisPRO compares your biomarker profile against trial eligibility criteria. Trials are ranked by how many of your characteristics match the trial requirements.
what_you_see: Trial name and purpose (in plain language)
Why this trial matches you (which of your biomarkers fit)
How to contact the trial team

example_matches.why_it_matches: Your MBD4 mutation may affect DNA repair, making PARP inhibitors potentially more effective. BRCA/HRD testing would confirm this.
Your MSS status means single immunotherapy won't work, but your PD-L1 positivity (CPS 10) suggests combination approaches may be worth exploring.
Therapeutic vaccines train the immune system to recognize tumor proteins. Your intact immune markers (PD-L1 positive) suggest your immune system could respond to vaccine-based approaches.
example_matches.eligibility: Ovarian cancer, MSS, prior platinum chemotherapy

data_shown.note: Specific trial listings require verification with your oncologist. CrisPRO identifies potential matches but does not guarantee eligibility.

stages.name: Treatment Fit Analysis
stages.plain_language: For each potential treatment, CrisPRO analyzes how well it matches your tumor's biology. This isn't just about whether you're eligible — it's about whether the treatment targets the right pathways in your specific cancer. A treatment might be technically available but not a good biological match for your tumor.

data_shown.how_it_works: CrisPRO builds a biological profile of each drug (what pathways it targets, what resistance it overcomes) and compares it to your tumor's profile. Treatments that target pathways active in your tumor score higher.

categories.fit_for_this_patient: Already received carboplatin + bevacizumab. Response completed but disease is advanced (Stage IVB).
categories.next_steps: Discuss next-line chemotherapy options with your oncologist

categories.fit_for_this_patient: Potentially strong fit IF BRCA/HRD testing comes back positive. MBD4 mutation may also enhance sensitivity. This is the most important test to complete.

categories.examples: Checkpoint inhibitor + chemotherapy, checkpoint inhibitor + targeted therapy
categories.fit_for_this_patient: Moderate fit. MSS status is a barrier, but PD-L1 positivity provides some rationale. Combination approaches (not single-agent) would be needed.
categories.next_steps: Discuss clinical trial options combining immunotherapy with other drugs

categories.fit_for_this_patient: ELAHERE requires FR-alpha positivity (>=75%). Your FR-alpha is negative (<1%), so this is NOT a match.

Exploratory. Vaccine approaches aim to activate the immune system against tumor proteins. Your PD-L1 positivity suggests immune engagement is possible, but MSS status means the immune system needs help recognizing the tumor.
categories.next_steps: Monitor clinical trial landscape for vaccine trials in ovarian cancer

stages.name: Resistance Forecasting
stages.plain_language: CrisPRO can forecast how your tumor might develop resistance to a treatment over time. Tumors are smart — they find ways to survive. By understanding the most likely resistance pathways for each treatment, your care team can plan ahead: which drug to try first, what to switch to when resistance develops, and how to combine treatments to block multiple escape routes.

data_shown.how_it_works: CrisPRO analyzes the biological pathways your tumor uses to survive and predicts which resistance mechanisms are most likely to activate for each treatment.

likely_resistance_mechanisms.what_it_means: The tumor may repair its BRCA gene, restoring DNA repair and making PARP inhibitors ineffective.
likely_resistance_mechanisms.backup_plan: Switch to a different mechanism class (e.g., immunotherapy combination)

likely_resistance_mechanisms.what_it_means: The tumor may produce proteins that pump the drug out of cells before it can work.
likely_resistance_mechanisms.backup_plan: Consider dose adjustment or combination with efflux inhibitor

example.strategic_implication: If PARP inhibitors are used, having a backup plan ready before resistance develops can save valuable treatment time.

data_shown.note: Resistance forecasting is based on published biological mechanisms. Actual resistance patterns vary by individual patient.

stages.name: Your Care Plan Summary
stages.plain_language: Everything comes together in a single care plan summary you can share with your oncologist. It includes your complete biomarker profile, recommended next tests, potential treatment options ranked by fit, matching clinical trials, and questions to ask at your next appointment.

roadmap_items.description: CrisPRO is developing the ability to predict whether you specifically will respond to a treatment, based on your tumor's complete biological profile. Currently, CrisPRO ranks treatments by how well they match your biology, but cannot yet predict individual response with certainty.
roadmap_items.note: Treatment fit ranking is available now. Individual response prediction is an active research area.

roadmap_items.capability: Real-time trial matching with live databases
roadmap_items.description: Currently, trial matching uses CrisPRO's curated trial database. Integration with live ClinicalTrials.gov data for real-time trial availability is being developed.
roadmap_items.note: Curated trial matching is available. Live database integration is planned.

roadmap_items.description: Automatic generation of a formatted presentation for your care team's tumor board meeting, summarizing your case and recommended options.
roadmap_items.note: Care plan summary is available. Tumor board presentation format is planned.
